name: How much does a garage conversion cost in Pasadena or Glendale?

mainEntity.name: What is the typical cost of converting a garage to living space in Pasadena, Glendale, or nearby Los Angeles neighborhoods?
mainEntity.text: What is the typical cost of converting a garage to living space in Pasadena, Glendale, or nearby Los Angeles neighborhoods?

acceptedAnswer.text: Garage conversion cost in Pasadena, Glendale, and the surrounding Los Angeles market depends on what exists today and how far the project goes. A basic habitable-space conversion is usually less expensive than building a detached ADU because you are working with an existing structure. Costs rise quickly when the garage needs structural reinforcement, new insulation assemblies, upgraded electrical service, plumbing for a bathroom, HVAC extensions, new windows, or high-end finishes. Older garages can also hide cost drivers such as deteriorated framing, damaged slabs, poor drainage, or outdated wiring. The most useful budgeting method is to separate the project into buckets: design and permit work, structural or envelope work, MEP trades, interior finishes, and contingency. Homeowners should also budget for possible soft costs like survey, engineering, and energy compliance documentation. Because neighborhoods vary in lot conditions and existing construction quality, two similar-looking garages can produce very different budgets. The best way to avoid surprises is to get a feasibility review before committing to a design direction. If the goal is a premium living space rather than a bare-bones conversion, budget for quality insulation, sound control, durable flooring, and a layout that feels integrated with the main home.
acceptedAnswer.description: Costs vary widely based on square footage, structural changes, plumbing, HVAC, and finish level. A basic conversion is usually much less expensive than a full ADU with kitchen and bathroom, but older garages, foundation issues, and custom design work can push the budget up quickly.
